design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: gate proof vocabulary has a producer
pattern: A gate proves each of its axes from a fixed set of canonical measurement names, and the modules that emit measurements each carry their own name table. Nothing relates the two tables. When no emitting module carries any name an axis proves from, that axis is structurally unprovable: every run reports it as not determined, the gate's overall verdict can never be reached, and no candidate can ever be promoted. Every per-module test stays green throughout, because each module is only ever tested against its own table.
docstring: Every measurement name a gate proves from must appear in at least one emitting module's declared name table. An axis whose whole proof vocabulary is unproduced is not a strict gate; it is a gate that cannot be answered, and the flow reports it as undetermined forever while looking healthy. The check is a set difference between two tables that already exist, so it costs one pass and it covers a name added tomorrow the day it lands.
fix_action: Build the union of the emitting modules' declared name tables (the physical sign-off source list, the power category map, the area taxonomy, and a name table the timing module must gain because it composes its names with a format string today). Compare that union against the gate's per-axis proof vocabulary. Refuse, naming the axis and every name in it, when no group of an axis has a single produced name. Report the same difference in the other direction as a warning: a produced name no gate proves from is a measurement nobody reads. THE PREDICATE WAS RUN, AND IT IS BUILDABLE AS DESCRIBED. Union of the four producer registries: 8 sign-off names, 4 power names, 14 area names, and 8 timing names that had to be EXPANDED from three format strings — which is why the timing module needs a declared table before the check can read it without a parser. Against the nine axes that union gives 2 of 3, 2 of 3, 0 of 4, 1 of 1, 1 of 2, 1 of 1, 2 of 2, 2 of 2, 1 of 1 — one axis structurally unprovable, and three more carrying a proof name nothing emits, which the axis survives only because a sibling group covers it. The partial rows are the reason the report must be per proof name and not per axis.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: required scope keys are emitted by their producer
pattern: A comparison gate declares, per axis, the set of measurement-condition keys two numbers must both carry before they may be compared. The module that emits that axis fills the keys it happens to have. Nothing relates the two sets. A producer short of one key makes every comparison over its numbers refuse, on both arms at once, before any value is looked at — and the refusal names a key, not a producer, so it reads as a caller mistake rather than as the emitting module's gap.
docstring: Each key a comparison gate requires of an axis must be emitted by the module that produces that axis, or that module must record, beside the scope it did not fill, the reason it could not. The two-sided rule matters: a key filled with an empty or null placeholder is worse than an absent one, because two placeholders compare equal and two numbers taken under conditions nobody recorded then pass as taken under the same conditions.
fix_action: For each axis of the comparison gate's required-keys table, construct the producing module's scope on a fixture and diff the key sets. Refuse when a required key is neither emitted nor accounted for by a recorded gap reason. Refuse separately, and with a distinct code, when a required key is present with a null or empty value. THE PREDICATE WAS RUN on the power axis by building the producer's real records and diffing their scope against the consumer's table: 5 of 6 required keys satisfied, the sixth missing. That is the whole check, on one axis, in a few lines — which is the argument for it. It must be driven per axis over the whole required table rather than per producer, because a producer emits scope for more than one axis and satisfying one says nothing about the next. THE RULE ALREADY HAS A WORKING REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION IN A SIBLING MODULE OF THE SAME LAYER, and the implementing lane should copy it rather than invent one. The timing producer declares a fixed key set that is ALWAYS PRESENT — 7 of the 7 its axis requires — and its suite refuses both a missing key and an UNDECLARED EXTRA, on the stated ground that a key nobody declared makes a record incomparable to every other record. The two producers between them evidence both clauses of this rule: one is short a key, and the other has been seen writing a key that is present and null, which the comparison refuses under a different code precisely because two nulls compare equal. Absent, present-and-null, and undeclared-extra are three distinct verdicts and the check owes all three.

design: plugin test suite, layer-wide; no design involved
rule_name: population guard asserts equality not a floor
pattern: A suite parametrises over a population it DISCOVERS (a glob, a package walk) but drives each member with an invocation it DECLARES (a hand-maintained table or a literal tuple). The guard against an empty population is written as a floor — at least N — with N frozen at the count on the day the two numbers happened to agree. The floor then passes forever while the two sets drift apart, so a member added later is silently uncovered, and an entry left behind for a member since deleted is invisible in the other direction. The class is not confined to test files and it is not confined to invocation tables: any place a literal list stands in for a population the code could enumerate has it, INCLUDING inside a census written to fix this very defect, which is where it is hardest to see because the file's subject is the rule it breaks.
docstring: A population guard over a discovered set must assert EQUALITY against the declared set and print the symmetric difference, never a lower bound. A lower bound answers a question nobody asked — is the population non-empty — while the question that matters is whether every discovered member is declared and every declared member still exists. A floor cannot see either drift, and it reads as coverage while holding neither.
fix_action: Replace the floor assertion with a set-equality assertion between the discovered population and the declared table, whose message prints both counts and both directions of the difference. Emit it ONCE for the whole population rather than once per member, so the reader gets the list instead of N single names. THE OBVIOUS WRONG GUARD, and one is already in the tree: asserting the declared table against ITS OWN length. That is self-consistency; it passes for any table and can never see the population. Assert against the POPULATION. Where several declared tables cover one discovered population, assert each against it and assert the tables agree with one another — the defect is not confined to invocation tables: the same shape sits on the present-but-empty input table and on the hand-listed producer set, whose discovered counterpart is an importable package. NOTE ON WHERE THIS LIVES: no program in this tree audits a test suite's own population arithmetic, so this routes to the gate that stands between a plugin change and a completion claim. Its natural home is a new member of the meta-gate family that already audits the program population for wiring and for a disclosed denominator; build it there and this gate calls it. COUNT THE OTHER SITES BEFORE BUILDING: measured on this tree the same shape sits on SIX tables of one layer — two invocation tables at 15 of 19, a present-but-empty input table at 8 of 19, a hand-named producer trio, a literal backend tuple whose package is importable, and the envelope-producer direction of the census at three literals. Only the first was known when this record was written; the other five came from asking the question once per table. A fix that repairs one table and leaves five is the floor again at a different altitude.

design: plugin test suite, layer-wide; no design involved
rule_name: layer membership is declared not inferred from a filename prefix
pattern: A suite that enforces a LAYER-wide property selects its population with a filename-prefix glob, because in the layer's first week the prefix and the layer were the same set. They stop being the same set as soon as the layer gains a module inside its own package, or a program that imports the layer under a different name. Every such executable is outside the population, so the layer property is unenforced on it — and the defect the suite exists to catch survives there untouched, with the suite green.
docstring: Membership of a layer is a RELATION — the executable imports the layer's package, or cites the layer's interface document — and it must be computed from that relation, never from how the file happens to be named. A naming convention standing in for a boundary silently shrinks the population every time the layer grows in a direction the convention did not anticipate, and the shrinkage is invisible because the members that fell out were never counted.
fix_action: Define the population as every executable that imports the layer's package or cites the layer's interface document, and take the prefix glob as one contributor rather than as the definition. Assert that the relation-derived population is a superset of the glob-derived one, and drive every arm of the layer property over the relation-derived set. NOTE ON WHERE THIS LIVES: same home as the population-equality rule, and they share a helper — the relation-derived population is the input both need, so computing it twice is how the two answers start to disagree.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: two input selectors given together must refuse
pattern: A tool grows a second way to name its input — a directory of many alongside the single positional one — and the two are wired as independent options rather than as alternatives. Given both, the later branch wins and the other input is never opened. Nothing is printed about the input that was dropped, so a caller who names a failing record and adds the directory flag is told the directory's verdict and never learns the record was not read. The exit code changes with it, from a finding to a could-not-check, which reads as an improvement.
docstring: Two selectors that name the same input in different ways are ALTERNATIVES and must be declared as such: given both, refuse as a bad invocation and name both. Silently letting one shadow the other converts a real verdict into a different verdict on an unrelated population, and the caller has no way to tell — the output is well-formed and describes work that was genuinely done, just not on the thing they named.
fix_action: Put the single-target and the collection selectors in one mutually exclusive group so the argument parser itself refuses both, and return the bad-invocation exit code rather than the could-not-check one. Where an existing caller depends on passing both, adjudicate BOTH populations and aggregate under the most-severe rule; never pick one silently. Add the both-given case to the layer's bad-invocation arm so every tool in the layer is covered by the same test rather than this one.

design: shipped plugin tree, any host; no design involved
rule_name: a runtime output path may not resolve inside the installed tree
pattern: A tool takes an output path from the caller and writes it as given. A relative path is resolved against the process working directory, which for a tool invoked from inside the installation is the installation. The write then creates directories and files inside the INSTALLED product, where they survive the run, appear as untracked additions, and can be picked up by the next hygiene or packaging pass as if they were shipped content. The failure is invisible to the caller because the write succeeds.
docstring: An artefact written on behalf of a caller belongs to that caller's run, so its resolved destination must lie outside the installed product tree. Resolve the destination before opening it and refuse when it falls inside the installation, naming both the resolved path and the installation root. The refusal must happen BEFORE any directory is created: a run that refuses and still leaves a directory behind has done the damage it declined to do, which is worse than either outcome alone.
fix_action: In the shared atomic writer, resolve the destination and compare it against the installation root computed from the module's own location. Refuse with the bad-invocation code before creating any parent directory. Two properties must be tested rather than assumed: that the refusal fires on a relative path when the working directory is the installation, and that after a refusal the tree carries no new entry — the measured case refused with the could-not-check code AND still wrote the file and its parent directory. NEAREST PRIOR ART, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH: a shipped guard already blocks a TEST RUN that leaves the tree it tests dirty, and it exists because three writers into the installed tree were each found by accident. It is scoped to a suite session and it looks AFTER the fact, at the working tree's status. A person running a shipped command outside any session is not in its population, and the write has already happened when it would look. Do not rebuild it and do not treat it as coverage: the new rule refuses at the write site, before the directory is created, on every invocation.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: a published absence claim is rechecked against the tree
pattern: A placeholder implementation carries an explanatory string saying WHY it cannot answer, and that string names a module or artefact as not yet present. The named thing lands later, in a different change, and the string is never revisited — it is a literal in a file nobody had reason to reopen. The stale claim is then copied verbatim into every document the placeholder publishes, where it reads as a current statement about the tree and is believed, because a provenance note is exactly the field a reader does not audit.
docstring: A published explanation that asserts a named artefact is ABSENT must be re-evaluated against the tree at the moment it is published, not written as a literal. Two qualifications decide the whole rule and both are structural. The absence verb must attach to THAT path — sharing a docstring with it is not attachment. And the claim must be UNCONDITIONAL: a message emitted only on the branch where the artefact was found missing is correct by construction and must never be flagged. What is refused is a claim that is published whatever the tree says, which is the only form that can go stale silently.
fix_action: Walk the string literals of the program layer. For each absence verb, take only paths within a short window of it, so the verb attaches to the path rather than merely sharing a docstring. Resolve each path; keep the ones that EXIST. Then discard every remaining hit whose literal is reachable only through a branch whose test mentions that artefact — those are correct messages on the not-found path. Refuse what is left: a claim of absence that is published unconditionally about something present. CORPUS-SWEPT ON THIS TREE, AND THE SWEEP IS WHERE BOTH QUALIFICATIONS CAME FROM. Matching a verb and a path anywhere in one literal gives 560 hits over 119,359 literals, all of them a module docstring naming a file in one paragraph and using an absence phrase in another. Requiring proximity gives 85 at a wide window, 14 at a medium one and 6 at a tight one. Reading those 6: four attach the verb to a different noun in the same sentence, and two are messages on a not-found branch. ZERO real defects remain, so this rule runs CLEAN on the tree today — the instance that motivated it has since been fixed at its one site. It is the only rule in this set that meets the run-clean bar outright, and it is worth having anyway: the fixed site was guarded by hand for one string, and nothing stops the next stub from carrying the next one.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
rule_name: a metric constant across arms that differ is not measured under that lever
pattern: A sweep turns a lever and records an objective on each arm. One axis of the objective is computed by a session whose inputs the lever cannot reach — it reads an upstream intermediate rather than the artefact the lever rewrote. The axis then returns the SAME value on every arm while every arm's actual artefacts differ. No individual number looks wrong, no gate fires, and the sweep publishes the axis as searched. A reader concludes the lever does not affect that axis, which is the exact opposite of what happened.
docstring: Across a set of arms whose implementations provably differ, an axis taking ONE distinct value on every arm is a candidate for not having been measured downstream of the lever. It is only a CANDIDATE: a clean design is clean on every arm, so a zero-valued count that is invariant is usually correct and flagging it is noise. The discriminator is a SIBLING measuring the same quantity from the same artefact: when one reading of a quantity moves across the arms and another reading of that same quantity does not, the frozen one is not describing the arms. That test needs no reference measurement and no knowledge of what the right value would be, which is what lets it run inside the flow.
fix_action: At sweep publication, for each axis over the arms that RAN: count distinct values and distinct implementation identities. Group axes into families sharing their leading name segments. Report an axis when the arms carry two or more implementation identities, the axis carries exactly one value, AND some sibling in its family carries more than one. Name the axis, the frozen value, the sibling and its spread. Raise the severity when the frozen value is a numeric sentinel, because a sentinel is what an un-analysed report prints. Two arms make it non-vacuous, so do not gate it behind a minimum sweep size; a one-arm sweep is skipped and SAYS it was skipped. CORPUS-SWEPT ON A REAL 21-ARM PUBLISHED SWEEP, AND NARROWED BY IT: the invariance test alone flags 24 of 54 axes, which is unusable — most are a clean design being clean on every arm. Adding the varying-sibling condition gives 8; requiring the frozen value to be a sentinel as well gives 4. Ship the two-condition form and report the sentinel as severity, not as a filter, because a legitimately-zero count with a varying sibling is a real pattern too. THE TOP HIT IS A LIVE DEFECT AND IT WAS FOUND INDEPENDENTLY BY ANOTHER ROUTE: a timing summary frozen at the sentinel on all 21 arms while its sibling reading of the same quantity spreads over 20 distinct values, from a multi-corner report whose corner key the comparison gate separately refuses as null. Two methods with nothing in common converging on one record is the strongest evidence either can give, and this method adds what the other cannot: the number itself does not move when the thing it measures does.

design: one routed digital core, open PDK; identifier withheld per capture honesty rule
title: A generated report header must be derived from the inputs the session actually opened
why_not_bucket_a: A program can decide this and the predicate is trivial — compare the claim against the input list — but no emitter records the inputs it opened, so today the check has nothing to read. The work is the provenance plumbing across every emitter, not the predicate, which is why this is a backlog item rather than a rule someone can add to one file.
pattern: A generated document describes its own basis in a header written as prose literals, while the session that produced it takes its inputs from variables resolved at run time. The two drift the first time a caller reaches the emitter by a path the header's author did not have in mind, and the document then states a basis the session never had. Nothing downstream can detect it: the header is well-formed, the numbers are real numbers produced by the real tool, and the only witness is the input list, which the document does not carry.
suggested_fix: Give every emitter a recorded list of the inputs it opened, and derive every self-describing line of the header from that list rather than from a literal. Then a single gate can assert, for any generated document, that each basis claim in its header is entailed by its own input list — and an emitter that claims a basis it cannot support fails at emission rather than at review. The degradation rule comes with it: when the intended input is missing, the emitter falls back AND the header, the stamp and the provenance envelope all name what was actually linked.
session_context: Raised while distilling an end-to-end drive of the measurement layer over one routed core. The instance that produced it has since been fixed in its own emitter by exactly this technique, which is what makes the general form worth building: the technique is known to work and is applied in one place out of many.

design: twelve arms of a seventy-arm cross-layer sweep, open PDK
problem: OpenROAD is killed by signal 11 during post-route design-rule repair, AFTER detailed routing has printed its own completion line, on every arm whose accumulator is non-redundant. Ten of ten such arms crash; none of the fifty-two arms that preserve the state encoding crash. The process exit is 139, the route itself completed, and the crash is therefore in the post-route repair stage rather than in routing.
golden_sample: ppa-crosslayer/records/trials/c02/ — a state-encoding-preserving arm of the same sweep, same tool build, same PDK, same script, which completes the post-route tail normally
bad_sample: ppa-crosslayer/records/trials/x03/ and x04, x11, x12, x13, y03, y04, y08, z24, z25 — ten reproductions of the same crash
tool_enhancement: Post-route design-rule repair must not fault on the netlist shape these arms produce; a repair pass that cannot proceed on a given instance is required to report that instance and continue or exit with a diagnostic, never to fault. The correlation is the lead: every crashing arm carries a non-redundant accumulator and no preserving arm crashes, so the reproduction is a netlist property rather than a floorplan or a random seed. Two properties the fix must hold: the ten samples above complete the post-route tail, and the tool exits non-zero with a named diagnostic rather than a signal on any instance it still cannot repair.
why_not_bucket_a: The fault is inside the forked tool's post-route repair stage; the flow's own classification and resume path already behave correctly — they name the crash, distinguish it from a routing failure, and re-run the tail with the faulting pass omitted. Any further plugin-side rule could only widen that workaround, and on two arms the resume already consumed the whole trial budget.
title: Post-route design-rule repair faults on a netlist shape after routing completes
pattern: A tool stage that runs AFTER the stage whose success it depends on faults rather than diagnosing, so the flow sees a signal instead of a message. The flow can classify it and route around it, but every arm carrying the triggering netlist property pays the cost of the workaround, and on the slowest arms the workaround consumes the budget the arm needed to produce a number at all.
suggested_fix: See the tool enhancement field: the faulting stage must degrade to a named diagnostic. The correlated netlist property in the samples is the reproduction path.
session_context: Ten of ten reproductions in one seventy-arm cross-layer sweep, all in the same design family, none in the fifty-two arms of the other family. Samples are committed in the sweep's own record tree.

design: the capture tooling itself; no design involved
rule_name: a writer enforces the field shapes its declared consumer requires
pattern: One tool WRITES a document and a second tool VALIDATES it. The writer's own schema documents a field as free text; the validator requires that field to match a fixed prefixed form. Each side is self-consistent and each side's tests pass. The writer accepts and emits the malformed document with no complaint, so the refusal arrives later, from a different tool, in a different run, and only if somebody thinks to run it — by which time the document has been filed and the author has moved on.
docstring: A writer that produces a document for a declared validator must apply that validator's field-shape rules AT WRITE TIME, not leave them to be discovered downstream. The two rule sets must come from one place: a shape restated in a second file is a shape that will disagree with the first. Measured cost of the split: the writer's own documentation gave no hint the field was constrained at all, so the natural reading produced a document its sibling refused.
fix_action: Import the validator's field-shape rules into the writer and apply them to every field the validator constrains, before the file is written; refuse with the validator's own message so the two tools cannot disagree about what is wrong. State the constrained shape in the writer's schema documentation as well, since an author reads the writer's contract and never the validator's. Add a two-directional test: a well-shaped field writes and validates, and a free-text field is refused BY THE WRITER rather than only by the validator.

design: the capture tooling itself; no design involved
rule_name: an accepted-value branch must be able to express its own vocabulary
pattern: A validator accepts a prefixed value and names, per prefix, the vocabulary the suffix is drawn from. One branch's suffix pattern cannot express any member of the vocabulary it names — every member carries a character the pattern excludes. The branch is therefore dead: it matches nothing, it has never matched anything, and it never will. Nothing detects this, because a branch that refuses everything looks exactly like a branch nobody has used yet, and the error message lists it among the supported forms.
docstring: Where a validator's accepted form names a vocabulary that exists in the tree, at least one member of that vocabulary must satisfy the form; a branch satisfied by no member is dead and must fail the suite rather than sit in the help text. The check is the vocabulary itself run through the pattern — a single pass over a list that is already machine-readable — so it stays true as either side changes, which is the only way it catches the case where the vocabulary gains its separator later.
fix_action: For every branch of an accepted-value pattern that names an enumerable in-tree vocabulary, run every member of that vocabulary through the branch and assert at least one is accepted. Report the branch, the vocabulary size, and the accepted count. Measured on this tree: the branch naming the flow's canonical steps accepts 0 of 42 of them, because every canonical step identifier is dotted and the branch's suffix admits only word characters and hyphens. Widen the suffix to the vocabulary's real character set, and add the census so the next divergence fails at the suite rather than at a filing. THIRD INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION, UNPROMPTED: while filing a record in this very batch I reached for the branch again — the natural component for a host-independence item is the flow step that owns it — and was refused a third time. An author who knows the branch is dead still reaches for it, because it is the correct-looking answer and the error message lists it among the supported forms. A dead branch is not merely unused; it actively costs every author who trusts the help text.

design: two committed record trees of one measurement layer; open PDK
rule_name: discovery selects on the parsed document not on the filename
pattern: A gate finds its inputs with a filename glob carrying a semantic token. The complaint the glob was written to answer is that a conforming record filed under another name goes unjudged — and a filename glob answers that complaint with a smaller version of itself. It fails in both directions at once: a conforming document whose name lacks the token is never read, and a NON-input whose name carries the token is read as an input, which for a gate that names its own output report after itself means the gate adjudicates its own verdict. The disclosed denominator does not save it, because the denominator is counted over the already-name-filtered population.
docstring: Discovery of typed input must select on the PARSED DOCUMENT — its declared schema, or where none is declared a structural predicate stated in the code — and never on the file's name. A name is a convention the producer may not have been told about, and it is chosen by the same author whose mistake the gate exists to catch. The output-document case must be excluded explicitly rather than by hoping its name differs: a gate that reads its own verdict as an input reports the pass it already wrote.
fix_action: Walk every candidate file under the root, parse it, and select on the declared schema identifier; where a document class declares none, select on a structural predicate and state that predicate in the code beside the selector. Exclude the gate's own output schemas by name of SCHEMA, not by name of file, and add a test that builds a real report with the real command, drops it in the corpus and asserts the vacuous refusal. Disclose three numbers on every run, not one: files opened, records selected, and files that could not be parsed — a file nobody could read is not a file that held no record, and it must raise the verdict rather than shrink the denominator quietly. Measured on the two committed record trees of this layer: 582 documents of which 15 declare the comparison schema, name-glob selects 0; and 496 documents of which 2 declare it, name-glob selects 4 — two records and two of the gate's own reports. A SECOND INSTANCE, IN THE SAME LAYER AND SHARPER: the timing module selects sign-off reports by a name pattern under three named directories, and its own comment claims that a new corner report is therefore picked up without a change to the module. Measured against the report names the flow's own runner writes, the pattern reaches 8 of 13 timing-shaped reports — and one of the five it misses is a report the SAME runner deliberately stamps with the basis marker this module reads. Some of the five may be out of scope on purpose; nothing in the selector says which, and that is the defect rather than the count. A structural selector states the intent it is currently leaving to a prefix.

design: any host carrying an older release of an optional dependency; no design involved
title: An optional dependency needs a version matrix, because present-but-too-old is the arm nothing tests
why_not_bucket_a: A program cannot decide this from the source: I built the static check four ways and every one over-reported, and all six survivors I could execute degraded correctly. The input that would settle it — the dependency INSTALLED AT AN OLDER RELEASE — does not exist on the host at check time, and no amount of reading the code conjures it. Producing that input is a version matrix in CI, and that is the engineering.
pattern: An optional dependency is handled for the case where it is ABSENT — the import is guarded, the fallback degrades, and that path is usually correct because it is the case the author imagined. The case that bites is PRESENT BUT TOO OLD: the import succeeds, the guard never runs, and an attribute added in a later release raises inside a program whose exit codes reserve a value for a finding about the subject under test. So a crash publishes itself as a verdict. Absent and too-old are different states and only the first is an import failure; every test that skips on importability covers the first and reports the second as an unexplained red.
suggested_fix: Add a CI arm that installs each optional dependency at the oldest release the plugin claims to support, and run the suite there. That arm is the only thing that can distinguish the two states, and it is what turns a red on somebody's machine into a red on ours. Alongside it, the cheap half is worth having: where a guarded import is followed by an attribute the fallback cannot supply, the fallback should set an explicit capability flag rather than a None, and the test-side skip should route through the not-verified tier carrying the remedy command, so the roll-up shows an unanswered question rather than a pass or an unexplained failure. MEASURED, and the measurement is why this is not a program rule: a static screen over the tree gives 131 guarded imports, 79 using an attribute outside the handler, 56 with no capability guard, and 8 once sibling and standard-library imports are excluded — and of the 6 of those 8 that can be executed with the dependency blocked, 6 of 6 degrade with a message and none crashes. The static form does not work. The motivating defect was never the absent case at all: it was an attribute that arrived in the dependency's next major release, on a host that had the older one, costing 33 red test identifiers and one crash returned under the exit code reserved for a design finding.
session_context: Raised while distilling a measurement layer's end-to-end lane cluster. Began as a Bucket-A static rule and was demoted by its own corpus sweep: four narrowings, all over-reporting, and every executable survivor behaving correctly.

design: one measurement layer of 26 modules; no design involved
rule_name: a contract relation is not an import edge and owes a pair test
pattern: Two modules agree on a document shape: one writes it, the other reads and validates it. Neither imports the other — the writer builds a plain mapping and the reader receives one — so the relation exists in the SHARED VOCABULARY and nowhere in the code. Dependency analysis cannot see it, the module graph shows the two as unrelated, and each side's suite exercises only its own reading of the shape. Both suites pass. The disagreement is reachable only by driving the two together, which nothing does, so the defect ships and is found by whoever first runs the layer end to end.
docstring: Where two modules share a document-shape identifier and neither imports the other, they have a contract with no code relation, and that pair owes a test that exercises BOTH sides — the real producer's output handed to the real consumer. This is the seam class that per-module suites cannot reach by construction, not by oversight: a suite that imports one module is testing one reading of a two-sided agreement, and a second reading it never loads cannot contradict it. Exclude the vocabulary token that most modules carry before counting, or the pair set explodes into every combination and the real seams drown in it.
fix_action: Collect, per module, the document-shape identifiers it names as string literals. Drop any identifier carried by more than two modules — that is the layer's universal record type, not a contract between a pair. Every remaining identifier shared by exactly two modules is a producer/consumer contract: require a test file whose imports include BOTH modules, and report each pair that has none. MEASURED ON THIS LAYER: 6 contract pairs; 0 of 6 have an import edge, so a dependency-graph check finds none of them; 5 of 6 now have a pair test, all added by the lanes that repaired the seam defects; and 1 of 6 has NEITHER — a live seam of exactly the shape that produced four of the eighteen findings. Guard the detector's own denominator: without the generic-token exclusion the same layer reports 47 pairs, and the 6 that matter are indistinguishable from the 41 that do not.

design: the plugin's own instruction surface; no design involved
rule_name: a documented command must be accepted by the program it names
pattern: Shipped documentation quotes a command as the way to run a tool. The tool's options change; the document does not, because nothing relates the two. An existing guard may already check that the named FILE exists — which it does — so the command looks verified while the invocation itself has never been tried. An agent following the instruction literally gets an argument error and no output, and the document that sent it there is the same document a reviewer would consult to confirm the instruction is right.
docstring: Every command quoted in shipped instruction text must be ACCEPTED by the program it names, not merely name a file that exists. Two extensions over the usual form of this guard, and each was needed to see a real case: the population must include the instruction surface an agent actually follows, not only the release notes and manifests; and the test must reach the OPTIONS, because a stale flag and a correct one point at the same existing file.
fix_action: Join backslash continuations FIRST, then extract each quoted invocation, then decide acceptance from the program's own declared options — or by invoking it in a way that can only fail on argument parsing. Report the document, the program and the offending options. MEASURED: 165 quoted commands name a program that exists; 11 use an option the program neither declares nor mentions; 2 of those 11 confirmed by running them, one reporting `unrecognized arguments` outright and both exiting on an argument error. WRITE THE SCREEN CAREFULLY — mine was wrong twice, in opposite directions, on this same corpus: matching greedily across lines bled the trailing compliance block into the preceding command and reported 47, and confining the match to one line excluded every multi-line invocation and reported 0, missing the one case already proven by execution. A checker for this that is itself built by grep will reproduce one of those two numbers.
